reasoning: A schema-local field inventory directly addresses the repeated bucket-placement and omitted-constraint errors. Clarifying exact-source matching helps distinguish a requested publisher from a similarly named regional edition and allows a source selector when no dedicated endpoint fits, without weakening the smallest-complete-call-set rule.

edits.target: Prefer an explicitly named endpoint when available. When the user names a platform or provider, treat it as a source constraint: use a matching endpoint from that source when it fulfills the request, rather than substituting another provider's generic endpoint.
edits.content: Prefer an explicitly named endpoint when available. Treat a named publisher, platform, or source as an exact source constraint, not merely a topic or locale hint. Use a source-specific endpoint, or a generic endpoint with a source selector that can represent the named source using a documented or unambiguous identifier. Do not substitute a similarly named regional or language edition unless requested, or use a broad search that does not constrain results to the named source.

edits.target: - For each selected endpoint, use only its own schema for exact parameter names, declared types, and required/optional placement; never borrow fields from similar operations. For parameters you include, put every required field in the required bucket and every non-required field in the optional bucket, even when the user explicitly requests an optional setting; never duplicate a field.
edits.content: - Before serializing a selected endpoint, build a field inventory from its own schema. Include every required field only in the required bucket, using a request-grounded or documented derived value; if a required value is unavailable, do not call that endpoint. Put each requested or clearly implied non-required field only in the optional bucket—even when the user explicitly asks for it. Map every compatible explicit constraint to its corresponding supported field; do not omit, swap, or repurpose it. Use exact field names and types, never borrow fields from similar operations, and never duplicate a field.
